preview: Nishant Patil shares his BNY Mellon internship interview experience, detailing the coding round, technical rounds, OOPs, SQL, and preparation tips.
content:
BNY MELLON INTERNSHIP INTERVIEW
Nishant Patil, Information Technology
Coding Round:
This round consisted of 4 questions
• A array was given in which each element was an array of format [nurseid,finishtime]. One nurse’s finish time can be the start time of next nurse available and the shift would start at time=0.We have to avoid overlapping as much as possible We have to find which was the longest slot any nurse worked in one single slot and return the nurseid. This is similar to n meetings in a room
o Test Case: [[0,8], [2,3], [1,4], [2,9]]. Here we can say nurse 2 did shift from 0 to 3, nurse 1 from 3 to 4, nurse 0 from 4 to 8,nurse 2 from 7 to 9. Longest slot was by nurse 0.
• https://practice.geeksforgeeks.org/problems/form-a-palindrome1455/1
In above problems I passed all test cases. I don’t exactly remember other 2 but in 3rd I managed to pass 3/11 test cases and in 4th I managed to pass 10/15 test cases.
I applied brute force in 3rd as time was running out and I wasn’t able to get optimized solution.
25 students were shortlisted for the next round

Round 1: (Hackerrank CodePair)
• Introduce yourself
• Explain your first project
• How did you implement the login feature of your project
• Explain constructor and its types
• Asked me about my second project which was a college laboratory booking website.
• Coding question:
o Given a string, we have to find total no of deletions such that all possible substrings have unique characters. Eg. String=”abaabcad” here we need to remove the three a’s and 1 b, total is 4.
This is simply a variation of no of distinct characters in a string.
Just find that and subtract from length of string
o Pair Sum
• Void pointer and dangling pointer
• Difference between encryption and hashing
• He also gave me a data where there were different countries give like India,USA and each country had a state like Tamil Nadu for India and Nevada for USA and each state had various cities like Chennai for Tamil Nadu and Las Vegas for Nevada. Which Data Structure could be used to represent the data.
I told that trees could be an option and also gave him an approach of nested map<string,map<string,vector<string>>>.
• He asked me my biggest achievement and my biggest regerets
• In the end He asked me if I had any questions to which I asked about projects during internship and the flexibility I might have. It is advised to always ask questions because it shows that you are interested in the company.

Round 2: (Hackerrank CodePair)
• After a my Introduction I was immediately given an OOP’s related question which would be difficult for me to describe and remember but it had a pure virtual function to be implemented.
For the first 5 minutes I was just scrolling up and down but somehow started moving towards a solution.
Interviewer after a few minutes said that you can just tell me the oops concepts used here to which I replied asking for 5-10 minutes if it was ok. He allowed me to try it.
I did implement the virtual function but the testcases weren’t passing as I hadn’t handled the data members input of the base class correctly.
Interviewer then asked me to let it go and moved onto ask oops concepts used here.
• He then asked me about JOINS in SQL and explain with real world examples use of each JOIN’s which I thought was commonly used.
I explained about natural join and left and right join.
Ps: Its fine if you just say natural join because even the interviewer was surprised when I mentioned left and right join. I mentioned it because on the same day I had attempted an SQL query where they were used
• He then asked me if there was a time when you felt this was impossible to pass through but you went through it.
• He asked me if I had any questions

That was the final round and I was one of 5 people to be selected

Preaparation Tips:
• 450 DSA for DSA practice. I would recommend to finish the greedy and dynamic programming section first. My order of doing it was Greedy->Dynamic programming ->Search and Sort-> Backtracking->Stack and Queues->Arrays->Strings->Trees and BST->Graph.
• OOP’S from JavaTpoint and CWH
• For DBMS Gate Smashers and InterviewBit
• For OS Gate Smashers and InterviewBit
• For SQL practice Hackerrank
• During the interview speak your solutions out loud even if you feel doubtful about approach. Your approach could be correct and sometimes interviewer might give you some hints too.
• It is recommended to have at least 2-3 projects on your resume and if they contain database it is a big plus point.
• Know everything about the projects you have mentioned in your resume. It gives an impression of lying if you arent able to answer questions related to them. Speaking of lying do not lie on resume.
• Even if you know the answer to the DSA questions tell the brute force approach first and then optimise it accordingly.
• Do solve the leetcode daily problems if you have completed a substantial topics as they will help you keep revised.
• Do give leetcode contests or Codeforces/Codechief contest. They prepare you for the adrenaline rush during online assessments.
• If you get rejected in a company, do the topic thoroughly which you couldn’t answer properly. This brings a great confidence boost and self belief.
• Lastly prepare consistently starting early and have faith in your preparations.
